title: Adults More Creative than Kids, Less Confident — Study
paragraphs: Many people believe that young children are naturally more creative than adults. But a new study from Austria suggests that this may not be true. Instead, the study found that adults produce more creative work, even though children feel much more confident about their creativity.

The study was carried out by psychologists Janika Saretzki and Mathias Benedek at the University of Graz and published in the journal PLOS One in October 2026. It involved 70 adults and 93 preschool children.

The participants completed three different tasks. First, they made free drawings without any instructions. Next, they made drawings that had to follow certain rules. Finally, they took a test that asked them to think of new and unusual ways to use everyday objects.
The results were then judged by five experts. Importantly, the experts did not know whether each piece of work had been made by an adult or a child.

According to the study, adults scored higher than children for originality, usefulness and overall creativity in almost all of the tasks. The only exception was the originality of the free drawings, where adults did not score higher.
However, the children had a very different experience from the adults. They enjoyed the tasks more, felt more motivated and confident, and showed less anxiety while they worked.

The researchers suggested that this may explain why people often think young children are so creative. It may be because children are so enthusiastic and confident when they create things, rather than because the things they create are actually more original.

Some media reports have described the study as proving that children's creativity is just an illusion. However, the researchers' own conclusions are more careful. The study only looked at three specific tasks, and it focused on how creative the results were and how the two groups felt while completing them.

Still, as one writer commenting on the study suggested, the findings may mean that adults are more creative than they think, and that what many adults lose over time is not their creativity, but their visible enjoyment of it.
